newsitem.title: USA: Innovex sees Q4 hurt by slower orders.
newsitem.headline: Innovex sees Q4 hurt by slower orders.

text.p: Innovex Inc said Friday that it expects its fiscal fourth quarter ended September 30 will not show the incremental increase in sales or net profits that was previously anticipated.
Innovex, which makes electrical components for the computer electronics and medical instruments markets, blamed changes in incoming orders.

Douglas Keller, vice president of finance, said the company is comfortable with earnings for the third quarter ending June 30 around $0.70 a share, which compares with year-ago third quarter results of $0.25.

Unless order patterns change, he added, fourth quarter results are expected to be flat or down compared with the third quarter. But fourth quarter results are still expected to be well above year-ago results of $0.27 a share, he added.
In a statement, the company said incoming orders from several customers for high-end magneto resistive (MR) lead wire assemblies are below levels previously forecasted.
The MR lead wire assemblies are used in disk drive heads for computers.

"This slowing in expected order growth has had very little effect on the current quarter which ends June 30, but unless order patterns improve soon, we will show little or no sequential growth in the fourth quarter," Thomas Haley, chairman, said in a statement.
Innovex said it does not expect current market weakness to continue into fiscal 1998, but rather anticipates strong market growth during the fiscal year.
